MosaiClusteR

An umbrella framework for multi-source and multi-omics clustering in R. One interface, many methods, and a complete workflow, from raw modalities to interpretable subgroups.

Get started Compare methods Reference GitHub

Why MosaiClusteR

Multi-omics and other multi-source studies measure the same objects through several heterogeneous lenses, and no single modality tells the whole story. The many integration algorithms in the literature live in scattered packages with incompatible inputs. MosaiClusteR gathers them behind one list-of-matrices interface (objects in rows, features in columns) with one return contract (DistM, Clust), so methods are directly comparable and the evaluation and visualisation tools work with any of them.

Direct

Concatenate the sources and cluster once. ADC, ADEC.

Similarity-based

Fuse per-source object similarities. SNF, WeightedClust, WonM, NEMO.

Graph-based

Partition a graph built from many clusterings. EnsembleClustering, HBGF.

Voting / consensus

Let many partitions vote, including the ABC family. M_ABC, CEC, EvidenceAccumulation.

Hierarchy-based

Consense the dendrograms themselves. HierarchicalEnsembleClustering, EHC.

Evaluate and compare

Score with ARI, NMI and Jaccard, and line methods up on the same footing.

60-second quick start 

# install.packages("MosaiClusteR")
library(MosaiClusteR)
data(mosaic_toy)                 # two sources, 60 shared objects, 3 planted groups
L     <- mosaic_toy$List
truth <- mosaic_toy$truth

fit    <- SNF(L, type = "data", distmeasure = c("euclidean", "euclidean"),
              normalize = c(FALSE, FALSE), method = list(NULL, NULL))
labels <- mosaic_labels(fit, k = 3)      # pull a partition from any result
cluster_agreement(labels, truth)         # ARI, NMI, Jaccard, purity

The same three lines (integrate, extract, evaluate) work for every method. See the method comparison to choose one, the animated concepts for how the paradigms work, and the guides for the full workflow.

The MoSaIC framework

A four-layer pipeline: preprocess, then single-source baselines, then integration across five paradigms, then evaluation and interpretation. You can enter at any layer, and every layer speaks the same List -> {DistM, Clust} language.

Install 

# the stable release, from CRAN
install.packages("MosaiClusteR")

# or the development version
remotes::install_github("lucp12891/MosaiClusteR")
